name: Sporulation Initiation and Spo0A Phosphorelay
description: Sporulation in Bacillus subtilis is a last-resort developmental program triggered by nutrient starvation and mediated through a sophisticated multi-component phosphorelay system converging on the master regulator Spo0A. The system integrates multiple environmental signals (nutrient depletion, cell density, DNA damage) through five histidine kinases (KinA-E) that phosphorylate Spo0F, which transfers phosphate through Spo0B to Spo0A. Phosphorylated Spo0A~P activates sporulation genes and represses vegetative growth genes, committing the cell to the irreversible sporulation pathway. This represents one of biology's most complex developmental decisions.
scientificAccuracy: This flowchart is based on verified genetic and biochemical data from decades of research on B. subtilis sporulation. The Spo0A phosphorelay is one of the best-characterized bacterial signal transduction systems. All kinases, phosphotransfer proteins, and Spo0A targets have been validated against primary research sources. The system's multi-kinase architecture provides sophisticated signal integration.

sources.title: Initiation of sporulation in B. subtilis is controlled by a multicomponent phosphorelay
Evidence that entry into sporulation in Bacillus subtilis is governed by a gradual increase in the level and activity of the master regulator Spo0A
Genetic networks controlling the initiation of sporulation and the development of genetic competence in Bacillus subtilis

notes: This flowchart represents sporulation initiation with 64 unique nodes (A-BM + ANDGATE1). Contains 6 OR logic gates (5 kinase sensors, Spo0A~P threshold decision) and 1 AND gate (high Spo0F~P AND low phosphatase activity). Demonstrates sophisticated signal integration through multi-kinase phosphorelay architecture. Spo0A~P acts as rheostat with three threshold levels controlling vegetative growth, transition genes, and full sporulation commitment. Irreversible developmental decision.
